lawyer:
Serajul Huq with Anisul Huq and Taufika Karim Advocates—For the Appellant
SA Hasan, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State
parties:
Gouranga Kumar Saha ----- Appellant
Vs.
State ----- Respondent opposite Party
full_judgment:
Ordinarily, hanging causes death by way of asphyxia when ligature mark is found on the neck if the body is allowed to hang. This is not possible through agency other than self. In hanging the basic presumption being that of suicide, the investigation starts with a feeling of handicap in pinning down incriminating element and factors. In hanging, the constricting force is the weight of the body, a fixed non-variable element. To enable it to efface compression, the ligature must be such as to slip up and hence the emphasis is on size and material. Certain types of cords, like coir etc., cannot be considered ideal ligature material for hanging because of spiky pieces projecting from them. Even too soft ligature, as of silk or soft cotton, is not satisfactory because of absence of steadiness in slipping and peculiar difficulty in the knot. The thin and somewhat rough ligature embraces and compresses the neck effectively. Thinner the ligature, tighter is the knot and there is more sustained suspension. The mark in such case would be deeper. 

 In the instant case the learned Judge found that the so-called hanging case as set up by the defence is absolutely concocted and a got-up story made only to hide the guilt of the accused. Once the guilt is uncovered i.e. the case of hanging is discarded by the Court, the accused is saddled with the burden of proving the facts especially within his knowledge as required under section 106 of the Evidence Act, namely," when any fact is specially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him." Since Ratna, the wife of Gouranga Kumar Saha was living with Gouranga in the same bed, and Ratna having received the injuries on her forehead and on the back which ultimately resulted in her death, onus heavily falls on Gouranga Kumar Saha as it is especially within his knowledge. Failure to discharge such onus, adverse presumption is bound to seize him. It is strange to note that accused Gouranga Kumar Saha did not identify the dead body of Ratna for making the inquest report to the police or himself did not lodge the First Information Report or he did not do anything which, as a husband is normally duty-bound. We cannot but agree with the learned Judge who found him guilty of the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code.
